newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia road, rail, air crashes kill 24,000 in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Russia road, rail, air crashes kill 24,000 in 1996.

text.p: More than 24,000 people were killed in Russian road, rail and air crashes in the first 10 months of this year and the number of air crash victims tripled to over 200 people, Itar-Tass news agency said on Wednesday.
But the agency, quoting figures from the State Statistics Committee, said the number of road crash victims fell 14 percent to 23,800 people.
It said 20 people were killed in railway accidents, three more than in the same period last year.

Experts have blamed financial difficulties for a series of air crashes in Russia in the last few years, with cash shortages further reducing already poor maintenance standards and placing extra pressure on air crews.
The latest crash was last Wednesday, when a military cargo plane delivering food to the Far East crashed in Siberia, killing all 23 people on board.

The fall in road casualties came despite a dramatic rise in the number of passenger cars in Russia. But death rates remain high due to bad roads, poor vehicle maintainance and reckless driving, often aggravated by drink.
